messages:
maya: Heads up — helm upgrade for gpupool-controller (v2.3.1) in us-west-2 failed because a pre-upgrade hook job never completed and left behind a ConfigMap with a finalizer. ArgoCD is now stuck OutOfSync and won't progress. Anyone on release duty?

deploy-bot: [helm] upgrade --namespace infra gpupool-controller v2.3.1 -> FAILED (hook: crd-migrate-job) at 2026-11-04T09:12:47Z : exit status 1

simon: Can you paste the job/pod logs and status? is it CrashLoopBackOff or stuck in Pending?

maya: quick outputs:
```
$ kubectl -n infra get jobs crd-migrate -o yaml
apiVersion: batch/v1
kind: Job
metadata:
  name: crd-migrate
  namespace: infra
status:
  active: 1
  failed: 0
  succeeded: 0

$ kubectl -n infra get pods -l job-name=crd-migrate
NAME                       READY   STATUS    RESTARTS   AGE
crd-migrate-5b7f8c9d6-xtz9p   0/1     Running   0          25m

$ kubectl -n infra logs crd-migrate-5b7f8c9d6-xtz9p
2026-11-04T09:10:12Z starting migration
... calling conversion webhook for CRD gpupools.infra.redwood.ai
ERROR: Post "https://gpupool-webhook.infra.svc:443/convert": context deadline exceeded
```

argocd-bot: App gpupools (infra) is OutOfSync: 3 resources. Sync blocked due to resource hook failure (hook.job/crd-migrate).

lee: Looks like conversion webhook endpoint wasn't reachable because the webhook service is on GPU nodes that didn't come up. Did terraform scale the nodepool?

anya: We saw a quota error in terraform earlier for us-west-2-gpu-pool — that would explain missing webhook pods. That incident also spun up a short burst of cloud costs when autoscaler retried last night.

ops-oncall: I can take this. Plan: (1) delete the stuck hook Job/pod so Helm can finish, (2) remove the leftover finalizer on the ConfigMap so ArgoCD stops complaining, (3) force a sync. Will coordinate.

simon: Be careful — deleting the job might orphan a CR that expected migration. If the CRD conversion is partially applied it could leave CRs in bad state. Prefer to remove finalizer first, then delete job.

ops-oncall: doing a safe sequence now. patching the ConfigMap finalizer:
```
$ kubectl -n infra get configmap gpupool-hook-output -o json | jq '.metadata.finalizers'
["migrations.infra.redwood.ai/finalizer"]

$ kubectl -n infra patch configmap gpupool-hook-output -p '{"metadata":{"finalizers":null}}' --type=merge
configmap/gpupool-hook-output patched
```

ops-oncall: deleting job and pod:
```
$ kubectl -n infra delete job crd-migrate --cascade=orphan
job.batch "crd-migrate" deleted
$ kubectl -n infra delete pod crd-migrate-5b7f8c9d6-xtz9p --grace-period=0 --force || true
pod "crd-migrate-5b7f8c9d6-xtz9p" deleted
```

argocd-bot: Triggering refresh for App gpupools (infra).

argocd-bot: Sync failed: found unmanaged resource configmap/gpupool-hook-output (created by helm hook); marking OutOfSync until removed.

ops-oncall: patched app to ignore this configmap temporarily via argocd resource-exclusions (will revert after). Then forced sync succeeded:
```
$ argocd app sync gpupools --force
application 'gpupools' sync started
application 'gpupools' synced successfully
```

maya: Nice work. Followups: 1) make hook idempotent and set `helm.sh/hook-delete-policy: before-hook-creation,hook-succeeded` so leftover artifacts don't block GitOps; 2) add a terraforms pre-apply quota check for GPU pools so we don't partially scale and break webhooks; 3) add a short timeout/retry on the webhook client to fail fast and clean up.

lee: I'll open a PR to change the chart hooks and add the delete policy + annotate hook-created resources with `argocd.argoproj.io/managed-by: helm` so ArgoCD treats them consistently.

anya: Also putting a note on the cost board — ephemeral failed scales are inflating the monthly GPU bill. We'll need an alert for repeated scale failures.

maya: filing a release postmortem + linking PRs. For now marking incident resolved for this upgrade. Thanks all. :tada:
